dashboard.label: REST API — Proxmox
dashboard.description: Pulling data from a system's REST API on a schedule (Proxmox virtualization, Berlin).

html.p: What this shows: instead of a device pushing logs, Splunk periodically pulls data from a system's REST API. Here a small script (poll_proxmox.py) runs on the Splunk host every 60 seconds, calls the Proxmox API (https://proxmox-berlin:8006/api2/json/…) with an API token, and turns each result into an event in berlin_proxmox.
This is the scripted input pattern — the standard way to pull from any REST/JSON API. Swap the endpoint + parser and you can ingest almost any product's API the same way.

search.query: index=berlin_proxmox sourcetype=proxmox:api | stats latest(_time) as last | eval last=strftime(last,"%F %T")
index=berlin_proxmox sourcetype=proxmox:api endpoint="cluster/resources" type=node | stats dc(node) as nodes
index=berlin_proxmox sourcetype=proxmox:api endpoint="cluster/resources" type=qemu | stats dc(name) as vms
index=berlin_proxmox sourcetype=proxmox:api endpoint="cluster/resources" type=lxc | stats dc(name) as cts
index=berlin_proxmox sourcetype=proxmox:api endpoint="cluster/resources" (type=qemu OR type=lxc) | dedup name | search status=running | stats count as running

index=berlin_proxmox sourcetype=proxmox:api endpoint="cluster/resources" | dedup type, id | eval CPU=round('cpu'*100,1), "Mem %"=round('mem'/'maxmem'*100,1) | rename type as Type, name as Name, node as Node, status as Status, CPU as "CPU %" | table Type Name Node Status "CPU %" "Mem %" | sort Type Name

panel.title: Running guests over time (watch it change when you start/stop one)

search.query: index=berlin_proxmox sourcetype=proxmox:api endpoint="cluster/resources" (type=qemu OR type=lxc) status=running | timechart span=1m dc(name) as "Running guests"

index=berlin_proxmox sourcetype=proxmox:api endpoint="cluster/resources" (type=qemu OR type=lxc) | stats latest(status) as Status, latest(type) as Type, latest(node) as Node, latest(vmid) as VMID by name | rename name as Name | table VMID Type Name Status Node | sort VMID

panel.title: Change guest state via the API (then watch the chart above)

html.p: Run from any box that can reach Proxmox (ubuntu-berlin or the Splunk host). It logs in with the lab creds (ticket auth) and issues the API call — no token needed. The next poll (≤60s) reflects the change here.
html.pre:
# list guests (get the VMID/name) curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/js-csco/splunk-dcloud/main/ubuntu/proxmox-guest.py | python3 - list
# start / stop / reboot one (by VMID or name) curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/js-csco/splunk-dcloud/main/ubuntu/proxmox-guest.py | python3 - stop 101 curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/js-csco/splunk-dcloud/main/ubuntu/proxmox-guest.py | python3 - start 101
html.p: Each action also emits a proxmox-ctl syslog event on the box it runs from, so the action itself is searchable too.

search.query: index=berlin_metrics sourcetype=proxmox:metrics otype=guest | timechart span=1m avg(cpu_pct) as "CPU %" by oname

index=berlin_metrics sourcetype=proxmox:metrics | stats latest(cpu_pct) as "CPU %" latest(mem_used_pct) as "Mem %" latest(mem_used_mb) as "Mem MB" latest(running) as Running by otype, oname, vmid | rename otype as Type, oname as Name, vmid as VMID | eval Running=if(Running==1,"running","stopped") | table Type Name VMID "CPU %" "Mem %" "Mem MB" Running | sort Type Name

html.p: The panels above use index berlin_metrics, sourcetype proxmox:metrics. They come from the same Proxmox API poll as the JSON events above — the poller just also emits per-node/per-guest CPU/mem/disk as key=value samples. Host metrics for all machines are on the Host & Infra Metrics app.

Collection runs on the Universal Forwarder on ubuntu-berlin (in-location): it pulls the local Proxmox API every 60s and forwards to the indexer → berlin_proxmox (so ben and gary see it; RBAC preserved). Install it with ubuntu/install-uf.sh.

Auth = ticket (username/password), no token needed. The poller logs in with the lab creds (root / cisco, in proxmox_config.env) each run and gets a short-lived session ticket — nothing to create, even though Proxmox resets each session. Override the target with env (PROXMOX_HOST/USER/PASSWORD) or $SPLUNK_HOME/var/lib/dcloud/proxmox.env if needed.
No data yet? Make sure the UF is installed on ubuntu-berlin and can reach 198.18.3.170:8006. (A central poll on the indexer exists but is disabled by default — see get_data_in/inputs.conf.)
